summary: Oil is back, and worse. Brent hit $117, the highest since June 2022 and above where it peaked at the start of this war. Crude is at $103, a five week high. Three days ago the story was US-Iran diplomacy. Now the expectation is that the US resumes strikes in the coming weeks. So much for the direction changing. Here is the part that matters. Yields fell anyway. The 10 year dropped 17bp on Thursday, the largest single day decline in more than a year, and sits at *5.00%* after a small bounce. The 2 year and 30 year are both down 10bp this week. Oil up 7%, the whole curve down. What does this even mean? I have been saying this for three weeks and this is the cleanest version yet: the long end is not trading on inflation. If it were, this week would have been a selloff. It is trading on where money wants to hide. Concerns about AI spending weighed on sentiment all week, and when investors get nervous about corporate credit they buy treasuries. Mixing this all in a pot: oil at a four year high, yields down, and the high yield spread at 340, the widest of this entire run. That is not an inflation trade, that is a risk trade. And the Fed? 91% say hold on Wednesday, 76% say hike in December. Add midterms in less than two weeks. Nobody wants to move first.
_fedPath_note: Every FOMC decision since the last hike, oldest first: the date, the upper bound of the target range after it, and hike / cut / hold. Drawn as the staircase under the Fed and listed in its card. Add a row after each meeting.

news.what: Brent hit $117, the highest since June 2022, on expectations the US resumes strikes on Iran. Diplomacy hopes lasted three days.
10 year fell 17bp in one session, the largest single day drop in more than a year.
Oil fell on hopes of US-Iran diplomacy. Housing starts dropped 5.2% in September and pending home sales hit a record low.
Market now prices about 83% odds the Fed holds next week, but about 75% odds of a hike in December. Warsh gave nothing away at the IMF meetings.
PPI hot: headline 6.3% YoY, the largest increase since December 2022. Retail sales +0.8% against 0.3% expected.
CPI came in hot. Headline 3.7% YoY (3.4% in Aug, 3.6% expected), core 2.6%. Gas +9.1% on the month was over half the headline increase.
Odds of another hike at the 28 Oct meeting jumped to about 50%, from 22% before the report.

_curve_note: Optional hand entry for a yield FRED has not published yet. Same rule as oil: only used while newer than FRED. notes/alert are display only. Put alert on whatever the day's story is: it turns the figure rust and is the only thing telling a first-time visitor where to look. strain is the quieter version: a smaller crack on the summit, number stays in ink. track is [open, low, now] for one tenor's day, drawn as a path under the summit; use it only when the path matters more than the close, and leave it out otherwise.
